checked_source_evidence.evidence: Confirms author, title, and August 20, 2026 version.

The chapter deliberately gives proof sketches and leaves substantial analytical justification to references. Omitted domain/approximation arguments are source gaps, not automatic consequences of the exercise wording.

The Dirichlet energy is the integral of the bilinear carre du champ; identification with the negative generator uses reversibility. These are background conventions, not extra exercise-specific conclusions.

The section assumes reversibility. In the Langevin specialization, Gamma(f,g) is the Euclidean gradient inner product, so E(f,f) is the integral of the squared gradient. A Euclidean Fisher calculation must be identified as this specialization, not a proof for every abstract semigroup.

The chapter-1 PI is written for f in L2(pi), with E(f,f) at least Var_pi(f)/C_PI. Operator/form domains are not fully specified by the sketch. Constants are projected out; centering is not a new final PI hypothesis.

For Langevin the PI reads Var_pi(f) <= C_PI integral ||grad f||^2 d pi. KL(mu||pi) is integral rho log rho d pi for rho=d mu/d pi when mu is absolutely continuous; it is not an arbitrary compensated integral over an unnormalized measure.

The density formulation is KL(rho*pi||pi) <= (C_LSI/2) E(rho,log rho). The text explicitly linearizes rho=1+epsilon*f for small positive epsilon and gives C_PI <= C_LSI. In the Langevin case, E(rho,log rho)=integral ||grad rho||^2/rho d pi, and the equivalent function formulation is Ent_pi(u^2) <= 2*C_LSI integral ||grad u||^2 d pi.

The exercise requests LSI-to-PI by linearization. Its hint assumes f is smooth, compactly supported, and pi-centered and asks for KL((1+epsilon*f)*pi||pi) = (epsilon^2/2) integral f^2 d pi + o(epsilon^2). It provides no worked proof of domination, density admissibility, energy expansion, or test-class extension.

Chapter 2 explicitly states both Euclidean PI and function-form LSI on all C_c^infinity(R^d) tests, without a centering requirement on PI tests. Its LSI coefficient is 2*C_LSI, and its PI coefficient is C_PI.

The chapter explicitly omits approximation arguments and cites Bakry et al. (2014, Chapter 3) for extensions. It distinguishes the direct Exercise 1.7 route from the route through T2. Proposition 2.1.1 assumes a bounded smooth centered f whose gradient has compact support; it does not assume f itself has compact support.

This proof takes f in the class of Proposition 2.1.1 and explicitly reuses (1.E.1). Thus the KL expansion has a second real source consumer on bounded smooth centered tests with compactly supported gradient. The transport lower bound and T2 are other ingredients of this corollary, not prerequisites of the direct LSI-to-PI route.

verdict_summary: The exercise's two textual regions are covered and the proposed direct perturbation spine is sound as a plan. The first compensated-integral packet is a useful, strictly smaller analytical prerequisite. Acceptance of the topology as fully source/domain-covered requires pinning the target test class, making the centering/extension order and LSI admissibility explicit, and recording the broader second consumer. None of these repairs requires widening the first packet to canonical KL, Fisher information, LSI, or the whole exercise.

findings.topic: Centering does not preserve compact support and extension is conditional
findings.finding: For an arbitrary compact smooth PI test g, f=g-integral g d pi is bounded and smooth and has compactly supported gradient, but usually is not compactly supported. Thus the literal centered-C_c hint cannot simply be applied to this f. The existing poincare-test-extension node notices the issue but its incoming prerequisites and conditional discharge are absent from the graph.
findings.required_repair: Make the bridge concrete. A natural route is to establish the bounded-centered KL expansion using the proposed finite-measure packet, prove the energy limit on bounded smooth centered functions with compact gradient support, derive a centered-test PI node from the two limits, then feed that node into the uncentering/test-class adapter. Alternatively retain a proved approximation bridge from the literal centered compact class. Add an explicit centered-test-PI -> poincare-test-extension dependency, or state the extension as a conditional implication and show where its restricted-PI premise is discharged. Do not add centering to the final PI hypotheses.

findings.topic: LSI application depends on which source formulation is assumed
findings.finding: The phrase 'valid positive test density' does not by itself discharge a compact-test LSI application. Even when f is compactly supported, sqrt(1+epsilon*f) equals 1 outside its support and is not compactly supported. If the assumed LSI is the chapter-1 all-density formulation, the normalized positive density can be used directly subject to its energy domain; if only the chapter-2 compact function formulation is assumed, an extension/equivalence bridge is necessary.
findings.required_repair: Specify the starting LSI formulation. Use either the all-density formulation with its audited domain, or add a distinct compact-LSI-to-perturbation-density source-gap node feeding the LSI/Fisher node. Record the exact energy formula FI/epsilon^2 = integral ||grad f||^2/(1+epsilon*f) d pi and its domination by 2||grad f||^2 when the density is at least 1/2. Supply gradient-energy integrability from the chosen test class; boundedness of f alone does not imply it.

edge_and_route_assessment.false_ands: No false AND was found among the recorded dependencies of the chosen direct perturbation route. edge_and_route_assessment.constant_check: With LSI written as KL <= (C/2) FI, the KL coefficient is (1/2) integral f^2 and the FI coefficient is integral ||grad f||^2. Dividing the applied inequality by epsilon^2 gives integral f^2 <= C integral ||grad f||^2. The resulting PI holds with the same admissible C; this is C_PI <= C_LSI for optimal constants, not equality of optimal constants.

hidden_assumption_check.measure: The standalone integral packet may use any finite measure. The probability KL adapter specifically needs pi total mass 1 and integral f d pi=0, since integral (1+epsilon*f) d pi = pi(univ)+epsilon integral f d pi.
hidden_assumption_check.positivity: A finite essential bound M>=0 gives an eventual positive lower bound, e.g. 1+epsilon*f >= 1/2 a.e. when |epsilon|M<=1/2. Handle M=0 without division by zero. Positivity follows internally from boundedness and small epsilon; it must not become a new hypothesis of the final LSI-to-PI theorem.
hidden_assumption_check.integrability: Finite measure plus essential boundedness gives integrability of f and f^2. The quadratic compensator needs a uniform measurable integrable envelope near epsilon=0. Canonical KL additionally needs its density/Radon-Nikodym identification and finiteness; the energy branch separately needs integrability of the squared gradient.
hidden_assumption_check.centering: Centering removes the linear term only in the probability KL adapter. It is not needed for the compensated finite-measure integral limit and is not a legitimate restriction on all final PI tests.
hidden_assumption_check.parameter_limit: The source's epsilon down to 0 suffices. A two-sided punctured real limit is a valid stronger analytical packet if positivity is proved eventually. No value assigned by a totalized quotient at epsilon=0 is evidence for the punctured limit.
hidden_assumption_check.extra_geometry: No log-concavity, strong convexity, finite second moment, or semigroup-decay theorem is needed for the proposed scalar/integral prerequisite. Do not import such assumptions merely because other chapter results use them.

first_packet_assessment.mathematical_boundary: For a finite measure mu and an a.e.-strongly-measurable real f with one finite essential bound, prove the punctured limit of integral [((1+epsilon*f) log(1+epsilon*f)-epsilon*f)/epsilon^2] d mu to (1/2) integral f^2 d mu. Equivalently use q(u)=u log u-u+1 and integrate q(1+epsilon*f)/epsilon^2. The compensator and normalization must be stated explicitly rather than left to an undefined name klFun.
first_packet_assessment.reason_useful: This is exactly the nontrivial interchange-of-limit-and-integral part behind (1.E.1). It applies both to the literal compact hint and to bounded centered functions with compactly supported gradient used after centering and in Corollary 2.1.2. The use is mathematical, not merely naming or wrapper reuse.
